_sources: WHO, Temperature Sensitivity of Vaccines (2014) - heat/freeze ranking poster
WHO SEARO, Immunization Handbook (India) Unit 4: cold chain - freezing points (HepB/Penta -0.5 C; IPV/DPT/TT -3 C)
CDC, Storage and Handling of Immunobiologics, Table 7-1 - storage ranges (MMR -50 to 8 C; HepB, RV 2-8 C do not freeze)
CDC, Storage and Handling Guide - reconstituted MMR use within 8 h
Participant Training Manual, Vaccine & Cold Chain Management (2023) - BCG, Penta 2-8 C, never freeze
Wikipedia 'Vaccine storage' summary table - HPV very heat stable, freeze and light sensitive
Heat half-lives (72/168/336/48/1000/672 h at 37 C) are CLASS-BASED ESTIMATES derived from the qualitative WHO ratings above. Verify against manufacturer package inserts before real use.

MR.name: Measles-Rubella (MR), lyophilised
MR.label_storage: -50 to 8 C; heat and light sensitive
MR.basis: WHO: heat sensitive, not freeze-damaged; CDC MMR reconstituted use within 8 h

BCG.name: BCG (lyophilised)
BCG.label_storage: 2 to 8 C; do not freeze; light sensitive
BCG.basis: Label: do not freeze; WHO: relatively heat stable (lyophilised)

PENTA.name: Pentavalent (DTwP-HepB-Hib)
PENTA.basis: WHO handbook: HepB/Penta freezes at -0.5 C; relatively heat stable

ROTA.name: Rotavirus (oral, liquid)
ROTA.basis: WHO: heat sensitive (OPV, Rota); freeze handling per product insert

HPV.name: HPV (recombinant VLP)
HPV.label_storage: 2 to 8 C; do not freeze; light sensitive
HPV.basis: WHO/Wikipedia summary: very heat stable, freeze and light sensitive

TT.name: Tetanus Toxoid
TT.basis: WHO handbook: TT freezes at -3 C; very heat stable (resistant to 55 C)
